newsitem.title: NORWAY: SOCCER-NORWEGIAN MAGNATES BUY BIG STAKE IN WIMBLEDON-NTB AGENCY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-NORWEGIAN MAGNATES BUY BIG STAKE IN WIMBLEDON-NTB AGENCY.

text.p: Norwegian billionaire entrepreneur Kjell Inge Roekke and close associate Bjoern Rune Gjelsten have bought a majority stake in English premier division soccer club Wimbledon, the NTB news agency said on Wednesday.

The business partners, who are also major shareholders in Norwegian elite division club Molde, paid 300 million crowns ($42 million) for the 80 percent stake held by club owner and managing director Sam Hammam, NTB said.
Hammam will remain as managing director and a minority shareholder.
NTB said the Norwegians plan to build a new stadium for the southwest London club, which shares the Selhurst Park ground with Crystal Palace.
Wimbledon finished eighth in the premier division last season after spending a large part of the season close to the top.
Roekke and Gjelsten have made no secret that they have been looking for an opportunity to invest in a top English club and last year looked closely at Leeds United.

The news agency said that Gjelsten valued the Wimbledon team at between 350 and 500 million crowns. It put earnings from television rights over the next three years at between 300 to 400 million crowns, in addition to income from the Wimbledon trademark, ticket sales and sponsorship.
Roekke, who divides his time between London and Oslo, is expected to play an active role in the running of the club.
Gjelsten is based in the Norwegian capital where he is chief executive officer of Norwegian holding company Aker RGI ASA, of which Roekke is the major shareholder.
The Wimbledon move is the latest in a long line of close soccer links between the two countries. Many of Norway's top internationals play for English club sides.
A spokesman at Wimbledon said the club had no comment at the moment. ($ = 7.138 Norwegian Crowns)
